name: CyTools_PersonaRP
description: Persistent characters: complete sheets, shared world lore, relationships, evolving dialogue, delivery annotations, and machine-readable scene descriptions for image and video tools. Runs locally.
author: Cyberalien

tested.runtime: Python 3.11.5, CyToolsCore 0.9.0, llama.cpp b11057 CUDA, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128, Qwen3-TTS 0.1.1, Whisper large-v3 turbo, Qwen2.5-VL 7B
tested.status: Executed: launcher from another working directory, Dear ImGui window on every tab, real CUDA generation, two-pass scene directive, multi-turn saved session, speech synthesis, a voice invented from a written description, a stable voice cloned from a 12-24 s take, Whisper transcription, a model downloaded and verified from Hugging Face, reference photographs attached to a sheet, appearance read from a photograph by a vision model under a decoding grammar, CLI and a real MCP stdio session. Linux and a published GitHub release were not exercised.

backends.description: Local GGUF inference on CPU or NVIDIA CUDA.

operations.name: Translate a scene
operations.description: Translate a stored scene, or a single text, with a language model of your choice. The translation is written beside each turn — the original is never changed — so a scene can carry several languages. Delivery marks such as [ton: ...] or [pause: 400ms] are masked before translation and put back afterwards; any the model loses are reported. The answer is constrained to one string per turn. Every request carries the context the words need, never translated itself: the world (genre, tone, setting, the places, factions and terms mentioned first), who speaks and how, where the scene stands, the lines just before in their original words, and your own note in context. A text given together with session_id is translated in the light of that scene, and nothing is stored. The places, factions and terms of the world read the same in every translation: each is rendered once per language, recorded in the world (term_translations; see translation_terms), required in every request, and a line that drops one is asked again once — termsMissed reports what still does.

operations.name: Speak a batch of lines

The list is sent inline: text holds a script ("Name: line", or "ID | Name: line"), a CSV or a JSON list (format auto recognises them), or items gives the lines as objects. Every line gets an id — its own, or its number — and its take is named after it. The folder holds the list as given (source.*), the batch as understood (lot.json), one WAV per line in voix/, and resultats.json / resultats.csv. The lines are generated many at a time in one copy of the voice model; with batch_size 0 the number follows the free VRAM, and a batch that does not fit is halved and tried again, so a large GPU is used to the full. A speaker is found by identifier, name, alias or a part of its name no other character has; voice names a stable voice instead, or on top of the character. A line that cannot be spoken is reported and the batch goes on. dry_run checks the list — speakers, voices, languages — before paying for it. resume continues an earlier task without generating its finished lines again. To read the list or bring characters from files on disk, use speak_batch_file.

operations.name: Create a stable voice
operations.description: Register a recording as a reusable voice. Every later line of that character is cloned from this take, so the voice stops drifting between replies and between sessions. The exact words of the take are required; they can be transcribed here.

attach.title: Attach it to that character straight away

for_language.title: Attach it for one language only
for_language.description: Empty makes it the character's main voice. A language makes it the voice of that language only — the main voice is kept.

transcribe.title: Transcribe the recording to obtain the exact words

voice.title: Stable voice

model.title: Voice model
model.description: Cloning runs on a Base variant; CustomVoice and VoiceDesign cannot reproduce a reference recording.

source.description: generated: built from a take produced here. imported: built from a recording you supplied. designed: built from a written voice description.

locked.title: Locked
locked.description: A locked voice refuses silent parameter drift.

voice.description: A reusable voice built from a short reference take.

operations.name: List stable voices
operations.description: Voices in the library, with their reference take.

operations.name: Verify a stable voice
operations.description: Check that the reference recording is still present and unchanged. A changed reference means the voice would no longer sound the same.

operations.name: Remove a stable voice
operations.description: Move a voice and its recording to data/voices/.trash. Nothing is deleted.

operations.name: Transcribe a recording
operations.description: Speech to text with Whisper, for a reference take or for dictating a message.

operations.name: List voice models
operations.description: Speech models and their installation state, size, licence and source.

operations.name: Install a voice model
operations.description: Download, resume or repair a speech model. The licence must be accepted personally.

accept_license.title: I personally accept this model licence

operations.name: Install the voice engine
operations.description: Create or repair the private speech environment (PyTorch, Qwen3-TTS, Whisper) at its final path, then import-check it. Nothing is recorded as installed before that passes.

operations.name: Release the voice workers
operations.description: Stop the speech processes and free their RAM and VRAM.

operations.name: List conversation models
operations.description: Catalogue with installation state, size, bytes present, licence and source.

verify.title: Re-check the SHA-256 of installed files

operations.name: Install a conversation model
operations.description: Download, resume or repair the weights of one catalogue model. The licence must be accepted personally first.

accept_license.title: I personally accept this model licence

operations.name: Install the NVIDIA CUDA engine
operations.description: Download and verify the Windows x64 CUDA build of llama.cpp, then test it against the installed driver before recording it.

operations.name: Unload the resident model
operations.description: Stop the conversation server and release its RAM and VRAM reservation.

operations.name: Diagnose
operations.description: Models, engines, devices, library counts and the storage layout actually in use.

operations.name: Update
operations.description: Check, stage, activate or roll back the application or the engine. Weights follow their own catalogue. data/ is never part of a replacement.
